newsitem.title: Morocco: Zaire's Mobutu and family due in Morocco.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu and family due in Morocco.

text.p: Zaire's ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko and his family will arrive in the Moroccan capital, Rabat, on Saturday night and stay in a hotel on the Atlantic coast, Moroccan officials told Reuters.
A Reuters correspondent saw unusual deployment of security forces around the Amphitrite hotel where the ousted dictator will spend his first night.
"The hotel was booked for Mobutu and his family... Therefore it is now not open to the public," a Moroccan official told Reuters.
The hotel is located about 20 km (13 miles) south of Rabat and close to the royal palace of Skhirat where King Hassan of Morocco receives important guests.

Another Moroccan official said Mobutu's plane was expected to land at Rabat airport late on Saturday night but gave no exact time. The official, insisting that he not be named, said Mobutu might change his initial schedule and land instead at Casablanca, 100 km (60 miles) away.
Zaire's rebels marched into the capital Kinshasa virtually unopposed on Saturday and their leader Laurent Kabila proclaimed himself head of state, crowning seven months of civil war.
As jubilant crowds turned out to greet the rebels after their marathon march across Africa's third largest country, Mobutu's rag-tag army switched sides, ditched their uniforms or fled.
Switzerland blocked all assets of Mobutu that it might hold in its banks and on its territory.
Kabila, in a statement read at a news conference in the southeastern city of Lubumbashi, said he was taking over as head of state with the agreement of generals in Kinshasa.
"According to reports from the generals, everyone was ready to take orders from me," he said.
Mobutu on Friday left Kinshasa for his jungle palace at Gbadolite in northern Zaire. One aide said Mobutu was still there on Saturday.
A Western senior diplomat earlier told Reuters that Mobutu was expected soon in Morocco, which is believed to be his final destination.
But a foreign ministry official said by telephone he could not confirm or deny the information on Mobutu's exile in Morocco.
King Hassan met Mobutu in Rabat last February when Mobutu was on his way to Zaire.

Morocco sent troops to Zaire to put down a 1977 secessionist uprising in Shaba after Zairean forces were overwhelmed. They also relieved French and Belgian paratroops backing Zairean authorities in the mining town of Kolwezi the following year.
